subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Redwood vs TitanAI
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@nexacare.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@nexacare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Redwood vs TitanAI

Hi Jamie / Samir —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the bake-off: 

Key pain you confirmed:
- Long tail latency spikes on your multi-tenant inference endpoints (esp during EOD batch windows) — currently 200–800ms variance
- High per-token cost for embeddings used by search reranking (~$X/token with your current provider)
- Need for predictable SLAs for scheduled reporting jobs and data isolation for PHI-sensitive traces

Goals you outlined:
1) Reduce median and tail latency to meet sub-150ms interactive targets for the CareOps app
2) Cut inference unit cost ~30% for high-frequency queries
3) Validate private deployment options for HIPAA workloads

What we demonstrated today:
- Redwood serving runtime with continuous batching and prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token cost
- Smart routing that can send critical low-latency requests to a hot pool while routing background workloads to cost-optimized instances
- Example SLA config and audit logs for private deployments

Open questions for NexaCare (please confirm):
- Are the Prod traffic patterns on the attached spreadsheet representative? (Samir — thanks for sharing the export)
- Which datasets contain PHI that must remain in VPC-only environments?
- What latency percentile matters most for user-facing flows (p95 vs p99)?

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood runs a short 48-hour synthetic latency/cost test using your sample traffic (we’ll use the test plan attached: nexacare-test-plan.csv) — Redwood to provide results and a short report.
2) NexaCare to pick 2 decision criteria to prioritize (latency, cost, SLA, data isolation).
3) Schedule a 60-minute follow-up to review test results and decision matrix. Proposed windows: Mon/Wed next week (I’ll send a calendar invite once we lock the time).

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-summary.pdf (summary of Redwood config used), nexacare-test-plan.csv (test inputs)

If I missed anything, shout — otherwise I’ll kick off the test tomorrow afternoon and loop Marissa for pricing/contract items.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

---

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nexacare.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@nexacare.com>
Cc: Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@nexacare.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Redwood vs TitanAI

Thanks Aditya — really helpful recap. A few quick clarifications: 

- Traffic export: yes, the attached CSV Samir sent earlier is the right one — represents a 72-hour slice from our staging cluster during a typical weekday.
- PHI: CareOps notes + anonymized patient context are currently stored in the same dataset; we’ll need VPC-only for any requests that touch the patient id field.
- Latency target: p95 is the gating metric for UI flows, p99 for critical alerting.

We’re happy for Redwood to run the 48-hour test. One ask — can you surface per-route cost estimates in the report (embeddings vs generation) so we can compare apples-to-apples with TitanAI?

I’ll confirm the follow-up time after checking calendars. Thanks again.

—Samir
Senior Engineering Manager, NexaCare
samir.patel@nexacare.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Redwood vs TitanAI

Marissa / Neha —

Forwarding the buyer note and their asks. Highlights for you: 
- Buyer will require p95 for UI flows and p99 for alerts (NexaCare will gate on p95).
- They need VPC-only for PHI-containing routes.
- They requested per-route cost breakdowns (embeddings vs generation) in our test report — please include our quantization + batching estimates and the expected unit price for a Dedicated pool.

Open items for pricing/ops: 
- Can we include a team-level discount for a 12-month Dedicated commit? (likely to move them away from TitanAI)
- Ops: confirm we can run a short test using a hybrid routing policy that demonstrates 95th percentile improvements (we should simulate their traffic mix from Samir’s export).

I’ve attached the redwood-bakeoff-summary.pdf and the test plan. I’ll start the test this afternoon (runs 48h). Please let me know if we should pause while you confirm discount authority.

Thanks,
Aditya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nexacare.com>, Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@nexacare.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Redwood vs TitanAI

Thanks for the forward, Aditya. Quick responses: 

Pricing:
- We can offer a 10% starter discount on a 12-month Dedicated commit; for anything above $200k ARR we have escalation to 15% with VP approval — I’m happy to own the escalation if we get close.

Test & Ops:
- Ops confirms we can run the hybrid routing scenario in staging and produce p95/p99 breakdowns; I’ve added a column in the attached test plan with the routing config we’ll use.
- I’ll prepare the per-route cost estimates (embeddings vs generation) and include expected unit economics under a Dedicated pool vs hosted.

Next steps I’ll take this week:
1) Finalize the per-route cost appendix and drop into the Drive link (will update the hubspot deal).
2) If test results look good, I’ll draft a slide with recommended pricing tiers for the NexaCare procurement team.

Aditya — go ahead with the 48-hour test. I’ll monitor and follow up with the report; looping Samir / Jamie for visibility.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
